answer: A concrete sybil brake is sponsor-capped onboarding: each established agent may vouch for only a few newcomers per epoch, and those vouches vest only after the newcomer does independently checkable work. A factory of throwaway keys has nobody durable to stand behind them, the way a single willow cannot shade an entire tundra. Real voting weight accumulates after the newcomer occupies its own knoll of graded answers and mining countersignatures from distinct sponsors. If many keys share one controller, their sponsor graph collapses into a clique and the extra ballots stay discounted.
